title: Thanks in all things (1 Thessalonians 5:18)
hookLine: not for everything, but in everything

lines: A WAITING ROOM IN THE NIGHT.
A CARD WITH A SUNRISE ON IT.
cards: A hospital waiting room in the middle of the night. Bad coffee, a television nobody watches, a phone almost dead. On the table, someone has left a card with a sunrise on it: give thanks in all things.
It can land like a slap. Thanks for this? For the scan, the layoff, the empty chair?
But the line is older than the card, from a letter Paul wrote to the church in Thessalonica, and read slowly, it doesn't say what the card seems to say. One small word carries it.

teach.b: Near the letter's end, Paul fires off short lines like notes on a fridge.
In the King James words: "Rejoice evermore. Pray without ceasing. In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you." In every thing. Not for every thing.

teach.h: IN, NOT FOR: THANKS INSIDE THE ROOM.
teach.b: Some readers put it this way: the hard thing is a room, and thanks is something said inside it. Nobody is asked to call the diagnosis a gift.
The thanks is for what's still true in there: a nurse who brings a blanket, a friend who answers at midnight, the breath you're still taking.
Another letter, Ephesians, speaks of "giving thanks always for all things." Christians read that in more than one way. Some hear trust that God can bring good even out of what hurts.
Others hear thanks for every good gift, offered at all times. Scripture doesn't hand over one tidy rule; the two lines sit side by side. Then there's Job.
In one day he hears that his animals, his servants and his children are gone.

teach.h: JOB TEARS HIS ROBE, THEN WORSHIPS.
teach.b: He tears his robe, shaves his head, falls to the ground, and worships: "the LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD." Look at the order. The torn robe comes first.
The grief isn't skipped to get to the blessing. Both happen on the same ground, the same day. That's the shape of in, not for.
The tears stay, and somewhere in the room, one good thing gets named.

how: Christians give thanks in prayers at meals, at bedtime and in church services, and a Christian funeral may give thanks for a life even while people grieve.

games.q: what does “thanks in all things” mean?
o: thanks said inside a hard time, without calling the hard thing good
a prayer said only after things have finally turned out well
a greeting-card saying that has no real source in the Bible

games.q: thanks in all things — tap the pairs.
p: thanks said inside the hard thing
giving thanks always for all things
Job, after he falls to the ground

s: in 1 Thessalonians, Paul says to give thanks for every thing that happens
the King James words are "in every thing give thanks." the small word is in.
Job worships before he shows any grief
he tears his robe and shaves his head first, then falls to the ground and worships.
Ephesians speaks of giving thanks always for all things
so Christians read the two letters together, in more than one way.

games.q: you're Job. in one day, messengers tell you your animals, your servants and your children are gone. what do you do?
o: tear your robe, fall to the ground, and worship.
say nothing and carry on as if nothing happened.
games.why: he tears his robe, shaves his head, falls down and worships: "the LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD." the grief comes first, and stays.

practice: Bring to mind one thing that's hard right now, and let it be as heavy as it is.
Still inside it, look for one true good, a person who stayed, a warm cup, a text that came at the right time, and hold it; you don't need to be grateful for the hard thing itself.
If you pray, thank God for that good in your own words; if not, let a quiet thank you rest on it.

wordCard.voice: Thanks in all things. Paul's line to the Thessalonians: in every thing give thanks. Thanks said inside the hard moment, without calling the hard moment good.

orig.note: Greek: in everything, give thanks (1 Thessalonians 5:18).

carryVoice: Your line: in, not for. One small word makes all the difference. See you tomorrow.
